name: tf-lab-two-independent-telemetry-authz
description: Meridian Capital trading fabric — telemetry-archive authorization tier, TWO-INDEPENDENT-AGGREGATE variant. The fabric exports two SEPARATE classes of data from separate loopbacks: a telemetry class and a metrics class. Each class has its own exporter on each switch, and each class summarizes to its OWN aggregate. The cloud archive must authorize both classes — and must authorize them as two distinct ranges. The two aggregates are independent: neither derives from the other, and there is no operational reason for one prefix to contain the other.

readOnlyDeviceService._whyThisIsHere: The harvest role reaches ceos1/ceos2 ONLY through a self-provisioned read-only MCP service. This document is topology/program reference data and deliberately carries no endpoint/category/tools fields of its own — so the descriptor below is the connection surface, and it must be named in the network pipeline's task description. Omitting it is not a soft failure: the harvest role is correct to refuse to invent connection fields, and the whole leg blocks at Phase 0.
readOnlyDeviceService.lifecycle: Self-provision per the active protocol: register from this descriptor, harvest read-only, then tear down the registration — on approval AND on escalation alike.

exportClasses.addressUniqueness: fabric-wide across BOTH classes — every exporter /32 is advertised, so a duplicate anywhere is a real BGP conflict
exportClasses.existingAllocations: NOT LISTED HERE — the pool already has scattered, asymmetric allocations on both switches, discoverable ONLY by harvesting the live devices.
exportClasses.independence: The two classes are operationally independent. They are separate export paths carrying different data to the same archive; no requirement exists that one class's range contain or adjoin the other's, and none should be invented.
exportClasses._theTemptation: Two aggregates invite being summarized into one. A single prefix covering both classes is SHORTER, tidier, and easier to express in a policy — and it is WRONG. Any prefix containing both classes also contains every address between them, which the fabric did not select and the archive must not authorize. Whether such a merge also swallows an existing allocation depends on where the classes land; that it authorizes unselected addresses does not. The archive must be authorized for the two ranges the fabric actually produced, expressed as two values.
exportClasses._whyThisIsUnarguablyRuntime: WOULD THESE VALUES CHANGE IF THE RIG WERE REBUILT? Yes — the scatter of existing allocations is re-randomized per build, so the free set changes, so the viable per-class selections change, so both aggregates change. No Program Architect can know them: the Architect reads only this file and requirements.md and has NO device-state access.

interdependency.chainedValue: BOTH derived aggregates, plus the four selected /32s and their class membership, for audit
interdependency.mechanism: the terraform leg's dependencyIds include its own approval gate AND the network sibling pipeline; the context-chainer PIPELINE-predecessor branch chains the network leg's report.md into the terraform leg's §6; the F18 settledness predicate holds the terraform leg until the network deliverable is fully persisted.
interdependency._whatTwoValuesTests: Every prior variant chained ONE value. Two tests something a single value cannot: that the consuming leg carries BOTH forward verbatim and keeps them distinct. A consumer that takes the first value it finds, or that collapses two into one, produces a policy that is wrong in a way no single-value round could reveal.
